title: The Elusive Quality of Integrity
text:
Integrity is an abstract notion that resists precise definition, yet societies rely on it when they evaluate public officials. Philosophers have traditionally associated it with consistency between stated principles and conduct, although critics note that this coherence can be achieved by stubbornness as easily as by virtue. The ambiguity has made the concept a rich subject of debate in ethics. Nevertheless, most people intuitively recognise a person of integrity when they encounter one.

Some researchers have attempted to operationalise the idea by measuring the gap between what leaders promise and what they actually deliver. Such metrics, however, risk reducing a moral quality to a checklist of observable outcomes. The deeper challenge, as one scholar observed, lies in the motives behind an action rather than its visible results. Until that distinction is resolved, the evaluation of integrity will remain a matter of judgement.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, how have philosophers traditionally understood integrity?
options: As a measure of personal wealth
As consistency between stated principles and conduct
As a result of formal education

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what risk do the metrics carry?
options: They are too expensive to apply
They reduce a moral quality to a checklist of observable outcomes
They can only be applied to elected officials

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of measuring integrity?
options: It can be fully captured by measurable outcomes
It is an imperfect task that depends partly on judgement
It is easy whenever leaders make many promises

questions.text: Which idea does the final sentence of the passage most strongly suggest?
options: Motives are irrelevant to moral evaluation
Visible results always reveal true integrity
Evaluation may improve once motives can be assessed more clearly

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being honest and having consistent moral principles
the quality of acting in the same way over time
the quality of having more than one possible meaning
the ability to form a considered opinion

paragraph_translations: A integridade é uma noção abstrata que resiste a uma definição precisa, mas as sociedades dependem dela ao avaliar agentes públicos. Os filósofos tradicionalmente a associam à coerência entre os princípios declarados e a conduta, embora os críticos observem que essa coerência pode ser alcançada pela teimosia tanto quanto pela virtude. A ambiguidade tornou o conceito um tema rico de debate na ética. Ainda assim, a maioria das pessoas reconhece intuitivamente uma pessoa íntegra quando a encontra.

Alguns pesquisadores tentaram tornar a ideia operacional, medindo a distância entre o que os líderes prometem e o que realmente entregam. Tais métricas, porém, correm o risco de reduzir uma qualidade moral a uma lista de resultados observáveis. O desafio mais profundo, como observou um estudioso, está nas motivações por trás de uma ação e não em seus resultados visíveis. Enquanto essa distinção não for resolvida, a avaliação da integridade continuará sendo uma questão de julgamento.
